name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,595

clue.text: Small, pale bird

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes a little bird with washed-out plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a large white water bird, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Queen wearing blue right next to group of soldiers

indicators.note: wearing means the colour is put on like clothing, wrapping around the queen
next to says the following pieces are simply placed alongside

blocks.note: start of sad, meaning blue or downhearted
Qu is an abbreviation for queen
end of sad
R is the abbreviation for right
on can mean beside, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: A queen dressed in blue stands beside a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue here is the mood, sad, rather than the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of cavalry or an air force formation, a body of military personnel.

clue.text: Confuse movement of a duck with taking off

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so that letter comes away from the duck's gait

blocks.note: a duck's rolling walk
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of how a duck moves before it takes flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking off looks like a duck getting airborne, but it means removing W.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle someone's mind or befuddle them, as in addled brains.

clue.text: Axeman might use this initially entering copse, trying resolutely to cut tree

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words
entering means going inside, so these letters are placed within the tree
the tree is cut into two parts so other letters can sit in the gap

blocks.note: first part of the fruit tree, split open
first letters of these four words
rest of the fruit tree

explanation.surface: A lumberjack hacks determinedly through a thicket to fell a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Axeman is slang for a guitarist, not a woodcutter; the first letters ECTR go inside PLUM to give PLECTRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist, nicknamed an axeman, strums the strings with this small flat pick.

clue.text: Unruly large women getting in beer on ship

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so this letter goes inside the drink

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
start of ale, a kind of beer
W is the abbreviation for women
rest of ale
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Rowdy, hefty women drinking beer on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On is a link here: the wordplay is on (placed after) the ship abbreviation in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungoverned and disregarding rules, a disorderly crowd is not under the control of any law.

clue.text: Aware of standing close to terrific girl, awake

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: last letter of terrific
a lass is a girl
awake and alert

explanation.surface: Someone senses they are standing close to a wonderful girl and is wide awake to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing looks like being on one's feet, but in the definition it means social status.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sharply alert to social rank and status distinctions between groups of people.

clue.text: Concerned about heat and dry? Frantically do this

definitions.note: refers back to being dry: the thing a dry person should do

indicators.note: acting frantically is wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
letters to be rearranged with the next word
letters to be rearranged with heat

explanation.surface: Worried about the heat and feeling parched? Then hurry and take on water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as advice to someone who is dry, which is why 'do this' can define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dried out by heat should restore lost water to the body by drinking fluids.

clue.text: Basic in some respects

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the following words

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of some and start of respects

explanation.surface: A qualified statement that something is elementary in certain ways.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'the mere facts', meaning nothing more than the simple, bare essentials.

clue.text: Don tries to break actual drill

indicators.note: to break something is to split it open, so these letters go into the gap

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
start of real, meaning actual
a judge hears or tries a case in court
end of real

explanation.surface: A university don attempts to disrupt a genuine training exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Don looks like an Oxbridge academic but is the verb meaning put on; tries is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A final full run-through of a play in costume is a practice, a kind of rehearsal routine.

clue.text: Conservative welcoming the man's idea

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the party word holds the other letters

blocks.note: start of Tory, a member of the UK Conservative Party
he is the man; the 's is read as 'is'
rest of Tory

explanation.surface: A Tory politician embraces another man's proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposed explanation or hypothesis is a notion or concept someone has formed.

clue.text: Below par when Arthur teed off - gripping end to game

indicators.note: a shot that goes off is wayward, so the letters are scattered into a new order
end to means only the final letter of the next word is used
gripping means holding something inside, so one letter is placed within the rearranged ones

blocks.note: fourteen letters to be rearranged
last letter of game

explanation.surface: A golfer called Arthur plays a poor round after a bad tee shot near the end of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Below par sounds like golf scoring, which is the misdirection; here it means feeling unwell. The rearranged letters grip E to give UNDER THE WEATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly ill or off-colour is an idiomatic sense of being not up to normal standard.

clue.text: Add seasoning to fish - European, posh restaurant might insist on this

definitions.text: posh restaurant might insist on this

blocks.note: to dress a salad is to add seasoning or sauce to it
a common sea fish
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A chef seasons a European fish dish at a smart restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The cookery words look like part of the dining scene but build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket restaurants often require diners to meet rules about smart attire, such as jackets and ties.

clue.text: Son - stir flipping drink!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word for stir is read the other way

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a stir is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent tells their son to stir a drink, with a mild oath.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping is also a mild British expletive, which hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonated water, or a fizzy soft beverage in American usage.

clue.text: Well-behaved soldier

blocks.note: first meaning: neat, tidy and disciplined
second meaning: a soldier who attends an officer or carries orders

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a description of a good soldier, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means tidy and disciplined; as a noun it is an attendant, especially a military one.

clue.text: Treacherous rogues and rebels

indicators.note: to rebel is to refuse to stay in line, so the letters break their order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about a band of villains and insurgents.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebels reads as a noun alongside rogues, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacherous ground or conditions are hazardous, full of risk and potential harm.

clue.text: "Labour with vigour" - a new catchphrase

blocks.note: to slog is to work hard and doggedly
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A political party unveils a fresh campaign line urging hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the British political party, but here it is plain hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorable motto or phrase used in advertising or politics is a synonym for a catchphrase.

clue.text: Rescue from deep river, swimming out of depth

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely and settle in a new order
out of says one letter is taken away from the phrase

blocks.note: letters taken as written
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A lifeguard pulls a swimmer out of a deep river where they were out of their depth.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from DEEP RIVER, then rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel or postpone a punishment, especially an execution, is to save someone from it.

clue.text: Adult who's lost east of American city, carelessly

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander into a new order
in an across clue east means to the right, so this part follows the city

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
NY is New York
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A grown-up who has lost their way somewhere in a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a haphazard, slapdash way is one sense of this adverb, as in 'thrown down anyhow'.

clue.text: Come off train

blocks.note: first meaning: turn out successfully
second meaning: exercise to get fit

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests getting off a railway train; both parts are verbs with different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to succeed or turn out well and to do physical exercise.

clue.text: Gold record-player with no ordinary remote

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so that letter is removed from the record-player

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a stereo plays records
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A gold-coloured turntable sold without a standard remote control.
explanation.walkthrough: Remote looks like a TV gadget, but it is the definition, an adjective meaning aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is stern, cold and distant in manner can be described as aloof or detached.

clue.text: Group of military vessels are made at docks - every stern

indicators.note: to dock is to cut short, and every stern means the back end of each word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Warships are built in the docks, from bow to stern.
explanation.walkthrough: Docks and stern both sound nautical, but they tell you to cut the last letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one that sailed against England in 1588.

clue.text: Food sent back - some chocolate fudge

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used
sent back means the found letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A diner returns a dish of chocolate fudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk is a kind of edible foodstuff.

clue.text: Cue, holding a rest

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so the cue wraps around the letter

blocks.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snooker player picks up the cue and the rest, the stick-shaped support for long shots.
explanation.walkthrough: Cue and rest are both snooker equipment, the misdirection; here a cue is a prompt and rest means what is left over. REMINDER holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over after part has been taken away is the balance or leftover part.

clue.text: Father adopting type of Buddhism, almost bewildered

indicators.note: adopting takes someone in, so the father word holds the other letters
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an informal word for father
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A dad takes up a Buddhist practice and is left almost baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: Almost applies only to the Buddhism word, trimmed before it goes inside; father is the informal word, not the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunned and confused, unable to think clearly, is a close synonym of perplexed.

clue.text: Ill-natured American police department

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces

explanation.surface: A grumpy US police department.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of a British police force, not an American one.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid remark is sharp and bitter, showing a sour, unkind temper.

clue.text: Angry talk to confuse what you're doing?

blocks.note: to be cross is to be annoyed
to have a word is to talk
to puzzle someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: Someone asks, after an angry outburst meant to bewilder, what exactly you think you are doing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the solver: the thing in front of you right now.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver is at this moment working on a grid of clued words, so the question describes the activity.

clue.text: Bare bottoms in England are very overdue

indicators.note: bottoms are the lowest parts, so in a word the final letters are taken

blocks.note: last letters of these two words
so means very, as in so good
overdue means late

explanation.surface: A headline about England's backsides being long overdue an outing, or a cricket side's tail failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleak, empty landscape with nothing growing is barren, stark and deserted.

clue.text: Unimportant fish in loch? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, here the fish and the loch
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the loch goes inside the fish instead

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite
L is the abbreviation for loch, as on maps

explanation.surface: A minor fish swims in a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: On the contrary reverses the instruction: not the fish in the loch, but L inside IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk or threats are empty and without real significance or consequence.
